title: Available Captures for Rook
summary: Given an 8 x 8 matrix representing a chessboard, count the number of black pawns ('p') that the white rook ('R') can capture by moving horizontally or vertically to the same square, without encountering any other pieces in the path.
statement: Given an 8 x 8 matrix representing a chessboard, count the number of black pawns ('p') that the white rook ('R') can capture by moving horizontally or vertically to the same square, without encountering any other pieces in the path.
constraints: board is eight by eight and contains exactly one white rook R.
White bishops B block the rook; black pawns p are capturable.
Count the first visible pawn, if any, along each of the rook’s four rays.
hints: Walk outward independently in each cardinal direction.
Stop at a bishop or board edge; count and stop at the first pawn.
Chess sliding attacks follow exactly these unobstructed rays, and each direction contributes at most one capture.
editorial: Chess sliding attacks follow exactly these unobstructed rays, and each direction contributes at most one capture.

tests.explanation: The rook sees one pawn above and one to the right.
The bishop blocks the upward pawn, leaving only the pawn to the right.
